organ: organ 2j, THE GATE TAKEN AGAIN, the mesh growing only by what beats the noise — on a dataset no attempt has touched, with each department offered in turn and seated only if the mesh, with it, leads the mesh without it beyond the noise on cases it may learn from, do the gate’s three tests hold together?
scenario: One real dataset downloaded after organ 2i was judged (data/fresh5-sources.json): the CDC Diabetes Health Indicators (UCI dataset 891; answers to the CDC’s 2015 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System; a stratified seeded sample of 59,999 of 253,680; diabetes or prediabetes; departments conditions 6 columns, habits 5, access 2, wellbeing 4, person 4; src/fresh5.mjs), a stratified 30% TEST, the rest 75 / 25 FIT / GATE. Each department grows 5 bodies on FIT (deep-quantile, deep-values, pairs-quantile, pairs-values, boosted; src/bodies.mjs) and fields the best on GATE; it is offered if that body beats a coin on GATE beyond the noise (organ 2h’s rule), strongest on GATE first. Offered in turn (src/grow.mjs), each department grows on its own columns and the scores of the departments admitted before it, fields the best body, and joins only if the mesh’s out-of-fold GATE predictions with it lead those without it (for the first, a coin) beyond the noise: the paired bootstrap’s 95% lower bound of the AUC lead above 0 (src/stats.mjs, 2,000 resamples, seed 99). A department refused sends no score and holds no seat. A score sent for a FIT case comes from a body that never grew on it (four folds by position). The mesh couples every admitted department’s score, linear or trees chosen out of fold on GATE. On TEST: against the best single department alone (of those offered, the best on TEST), the same admitted departments answering alone, one score each, coupled the same way, a coupling taught shuffled outcomes, random routing, boosted trees and logistic regression on every column pooled, and, on 1,200 cases (400 with the outcome, 800 without, seeded), Claude Opus 5.5 asked cold in four batches of 300, each batch a fresh subagent that reads only its prompt (tools/contest-2j.mjs), shown the same 21 columns the departments hold between them. Also recorded and not a rule: the mesh organ 2i’s rule would have grown here, every offered department joined in the same order.

rules.claim: the fresh file is the one downloaded, byte for byte; each department reads only its own columns and the scores of departments admitted before it, TEST is never read (scrambling every TEST record leaves every department’s bodies, the body it fields, whether it is offered, the order, each join with its lead and bound, what each department was sent, and the mesh’s choice of coupling unchanged), a changed seed is refused before it is read, the frontier model is shown exactly the columns the departments hold, and it answered every batch of 300 to its sealed prompt (1,200 cases)
rules.seenBeforeSeal: the fresh file’s row count (253,680), each column’s range against the survey’s codebook, and the sample and split sizes (59,999; FIT 31,500, GATE 10,500, TEST 17,999), checked by the loader’s tests; the design record data/diagnose-8.json (organ 2i’s domains, FIT and GATE only). A dry run on GitHub’s runner grew and scored on the fresh data with synthetic frontier answers and printed only whether it ran; no other model was grown or scored on it before this seal

rules.claim: COMPOSITION > PARTS: at least two departments join, and the mesh beats its best single department alone on TEST (the best on TEST of those offered): bound above 0
APPROACHES THE FRONTIER: on the 1,200, the mesh is not worse than the frontier model by more than 0.02 AUC: bound above −0.02

GROWTH MEASURABLY RAISES IT: with at least two departments joined, adding them one at a time in the order they joined (the coupling chosen afresh at each size) never lowers the TEST AUC, and the full mesh beats its first department beyond the noise: bound above 0
APPROACHES THE POURED MONOLITH: the mesh is not worse than boosted trees on every column pooled in one place by more than 0.02 AUC: bound above −0.02
NOT A SHAM: the mesh beats a coupling taught shuffled outcomes and random routing (both bounds above 0), and grown on shuffled outcomes no department is offered
THE RELAY ADDS: with at least two departments joined, the mesh beats the same departments answering alone, one score each, coupled the same way: bound above 0
THE GATE, the spec’s WIN in full: R2, R3 and R4 all hold. Nothing below the gate (organs 3 to 7) is sealed unless it does

disclosure: Sealed after organ 2i was judged, knowing every number of organs 2 to 2i and the checks after them. In 2i, on the hotel bookings and the news articles, the mesh beat its parts, came out ahead of the frontier model in both beyond the noise, came within 0.02 of every record pooled, and the relay added; the gate failed on growth alone: on the news articles the sixth department to join raised the mesh’s out-of-fold GATE score by 0.0013 and lowered TEST by 0.0011. The first fix designed, a join on any gain at all on GATE (src/join.mjs), would have admitted every department in both domains and changed nothing (data/diagnose-7.json), so it was dropped before any seal. This one asks a department to lead beyond the noise of the cases it is measured on, by the same bound every claim here is judged by, and makes the relay and the join one step, so a department refused sends no score. On organ 2i’s own domains, on FIT and GATE alone (data/diagnose-8.json, TEST never read), on the hotel bookings it admitted guests, sales, reservations, stay, refusing none; on the news articles it admitted keywords, desk, links, writing and refused topics (GATE 0.717346 → 0.718141, bound -0.00105), tone (GATE 0.720539 → 0.721921, bound -0.000327). Those domains’ TEST results were seen in 2i, so that is a check of what the rule does, not of whether it works; this seal predicts on a domain no organ has scored. Everything else is 2i’s: the bodies, how a department is offered, the coupling, the rivals, the frontier test on 1,200 cases, growth that must be measurable; R4 is judged on the departments that joined, in the order they joined. The expectations written before the run: R2, R4 and R6 hold; R3 is open, since the frontier model knows what high blood pressure, a high body mass index and poor general health mean for diabetes, and here it sees every column the departments do; R5 is open; R7 is open, since the relay paid on the hotel bookings and the news articles, which are not these. The survey’s answers are anonymised by the CDC; identical answers can fall on both sides of the split, for every model alike. The seal pins data/fresh5-sources.json, which holds the fresh file’s hash, and the measurement refuses to run if the file differs from it.
